newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures finish higher.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures finish higher.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures finished higher, with marks and Swiss francs ending near the day's highs after ignoring bearish comments throughout the day, traders and analysts said.
June marks closed near the session high of $0.6016, which corresponds to a key support level in dollar/mark at 1.6720 spot, despite comments from the head of the International Monetary Fund.
IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus argued against any delay in the planned 1999 launch of a new European currency, saying it was time "to finish the job" of monetary union.
The statements were opposite of comments made overnight by Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher.
Kuehbacher expressed doubts that Germany could meet the Maastricht criteria, which immediately sparked demand for marks against most currencies.
Camdessus also suggested Europe consider interest rate cuts if growth falters, and said persistently higher EU unemployment could undermine the Euro's stability.
"He is saying a weak Euro is in store for the EMU," one currency trader said about Camdessus's comments.
"The only way to lead Europe's economies out of the doldrums is through the export side, and that means lowering the value of the currency," he said.

However, the comments barely registered in the trading pits. Rather, futures price activity reflected technical buying, as well as continued unwinding in the cash markets of short mark trades against most currencies, including the dollar.
Traders said both mark and Swiss franc futures were oversold and would continue to find technical buying.

The technical resiliency of the contracts was witnessed early when June Swiss francs rallied sharply even though Swiss National Bank chairman Hans Meyer said that the SNB planned to keep policy expansive for the foreseeable future.
Meyer also played down fears the policy could be fueling inflation, noting that Switzerland's production potential remained well below capacity.
"That should have knocked Swiss lower," a trader said.
Meanwhile, Canadian dollar futures expanded losses, with June coming closer to key support at $0.7300.
"Below $0.7300, it will be carnage," one pit trader said.
Despite declines in Australian dollar futures, traders noted active June Aussie dollar buying against June Canadian dollar contracts.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was up $0.000075 at $0.008267, marks were up $0.0062 at $0.6011, Swiss francs were $0.0101 higher at $0.7014, sterling were up $0.0012 at $1.5868, Canadian dollars were down $0.0018 at $0.7324, Australian dollars were $0.0041 lower at $0.7880 and Mexican pesos were $0.000675 higher at $0.121050.
